title: UMMC adds six seats to Mississippi’s only dental school
excerpt: UMMC’s incoming dentistry class grew from 40 to 46. Prospective dentists can look for preview-day details in January. Northeast lists May 1 for dental hygiene applications.

facts.statement: Mississippi’s only dental school has expanded its entering class from 40 students to 46. The University of Mississippi Medical Center said Monday that two members of the class of 2030 are from Arkansas, the first out-of-state students it has admitted. The school will consider Arkansas applicants one year at a time.

paragraphs.text: Mississippi’s only dental school has expanded its entering class from 40 students to 46. The University of Mississippi Medical Center said Monday that two members of the class of 2030 are from Arkansas, the first out-of-state students it has admitted. The school will consider Arkansas applicants one year at a time.

A new clinical building under construction in Jackson could eventually give the school room for 50 students per class, according to Dean Pia Chatterjee Kirk. Plans include a clinic for dental residents and private practice space. UMMC is also considering admitting more dental hygiene students once clinical operations free up space in its existing building.

Pontotoc-area students considering a Doctor of Dental Medicine degree can watch for UMMC to announce preview days in January. Prospective students can meet admissions directors at those events. UMMC directs applicants to submit transcripts and recommendations through the national dental school application service.

For students interested in becoming dental hygienists, Northeast Mississippi Community College in Booneville has posted a May 1 deadline for its fall 2027 application. The college lists its application and program director’s contact information on its dental hygiene page.
